chapter: Jazz at the Philharmonic and the record business
title: Recording for anyone: Eddie Laguna's Sunset label and Al Benson
summary: He demanded his own price and was cheated by Al Benson over Acoustic Records masters.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Right before that, or in the same period, after the record ban was over, so many new companies cropped up. You did some things for that...
See, I recorded for anybody and everybody that had a label.
What was that thing with Willie Smith and Lucky Thompson...?
Yeah. He was one of the ones I got, too. Ha-ha! I mean, I made him give me what I wanted.
Sunset, that was the name of the label.

Yeah, the Sunset label. Yeah, they were giving everybody... They said, "Well, we pay so-and-so-so." I said, "Well, I don't care what you pay them. You pay me such-and-such amount." And that's the only way I could get any money out of the deal! If I had to go along with their program, they'd hand me scale and say, "Yeah, thanks," and shit, they ain't givin' you nothing! You got to speak up for yourself, or else you don't get nothin'.
And wasn't there a thing with Al Benson in Chicago that you told me about?

Yeah, Al Benson got to me, too. But I mean, he was slick. He waited til I left Chicago, and I didn't know about it... Acoustic Records. I had recorded for them, but I didn't know they was goin' out of business. So they didn't pay me for the date, and Al Benson got the masters because I wasn't there to protest against it. Because they owed me money... And he couldn't have got them if I had been in Chicago at the time telling the judge, "Well, Judge, they owe me for this."
So it should have reverted to me.

To me, yeah. And it would have come back to me, you know. But Al Benson said, "Oh, well, he owes me money," so he got the record. And the next thing I know is that they're on the market, and he sold them to somebody
else, and somebody else did it or something. Anyway, they got me; I didn't get paid for those things.
